# Consensus Algorithms: Raft vs. Paxos vs. PBFT

## 1. Problem Framing

### The Consensus Problem
Consensus is the challenge of getting a distributed system of independent nodes to **agree on a single value or sequence of values**, even when:
- Nodes crash and recover
- Network partitions occur
- Messages are delayed or lost

### Why Consensus Is Hard
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    FLP Impossibility                        │
│                                                             │
│  In a fully asynchronous system, no deterministic          │
│  consensus algorithm can guarantee both safety AND liveness │
│  if even a single node can fail.                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Core Requirements (Any Consensus Protocol Must Provide)
| Requirement | Definition |
|-------------|------------|
| **Agreement** | All non-faulty nodes decide on the same value |
| **Validity** | The decided value must have been proposed by some node |
| **Termination** | Every non-faulty node eventually decides a value |
| **Integrity** | A node decides at most once |
